title: Co-Manager Permission Conflicts and Data Consistency Validation
user_story: As a League Commissioner, I want the system to prevent and resolve co-manager permission conflicts, so that when multiple co-managers edit team data concurrently, historical statistics are attributed correctly, permission hierarchies are enforced, and no data inconsistencies occur that could corrupt league records.
problem_statement: When multiple co-managers have permission to edit the same team (e.g., two people managing 'Team Alpha'), concurrent edits can create data conflicts: lineup changes overwriting each other, trade proposals duplicated, or historical statistics incorrectly attributed to the wrong manager. Without clear permission hierarchy (which co-manager's action takes precedence?) and conflict resolution mechanisms, teams with multiple managers become data consistency risks. Additionally, if a co-manager is removed mid-season, their historical contributions must be preserved while future access is revoked.

business_value.data_integrity: Prevent data corruption and inconsistencies in multi-manager scenarios
business_value.user_trust: Ensure co-managers can collaborate without fear of overwriting each other's work
business_value.audit_compliance: Maintain accurate historical attribution of all team actions for league records
business_value.scalability: Enable advanced league configurations with multiple managers per team

criteria: GIVEN team has multiple co-managers with same role ('manager' or 'co-manager')
WHEN defining permission hierarchy
THEN system establishes precedence: (1) Primary Manager (first user assigned to team), (2) Co-Managers (ordered by date added), (3) Commissioner (can override all)
AND primary manager cannot be removed unless reassigned to another user (prevents orphaned teams)
AND permission hierarchy is visible in team management UI: 'Primary Manager: User A, Co-Managers: User B (added 2024-08-01), User C (added 2024-09-15)'
AND API returns 'manager_role' field with values: 'primary' | 'co-manager' | 'commissioner-override'

acceptance_criteria.description: Concurrent Edit Detection via Optimistic Locking
criteria: GIVEN two co-managers edit same team entity (lineup, roster, team name) simultaneously
WHEN both submit changes within <10 second window
THEN system uses optimistic locking: each entity has 'version' field (integer, increments on each update)
AND first edit to acquire lock succeeds, increments version
AND second edit detects version mismatch, rejects with error: 'Team data was updated by another manager. Refresh and reapply your changes.'
AND rejected user receives notification with diff showing conflicting changes: 'User B changed Lineup Slot 1 from Player X to Player Y while you were editing'
AND system provides 'Merge Changes' option if conflicts are in different fields (e.g., one changed lineup, other changed team name)
GIVEN co-manager is actively editing team (has edit form open)
WHEN another co-manager opens same edit form
THEN system displays banner: 'User B is currently editing this team. Changes may conflict.'
AND UI shows 'active editor' badge next to fields being edited (e.g., 'Lineup: User B is editing...')
AND real-time sync via WebSocket updates form fields as other user makes changes (live collaboration, like Google Docs)
AND if edit session inactive for >5 minutes, 'active editor' lock released automatically
GIVEN co-manager makes team action (sets lineup, proposes trade, changes team name)
WHEN action is recorded
THEN system stores attribution metadata: (1) 'action_by_user_id', (2) 'action_timestamp', (3) 'action_type', (4) 'manager_role_at_time' (primary/co-manager/commissioner)
AND historical records display: 'Lineup set by User B (Co-Manager) on 2024-09-15 at 2:45 PM'
AND if co-manager is later removed, historical records still show their name/role at time of action (not 'Unknown User')
AND API endpoint GET /teams/:id/action-history returns full attribution details for all past actions
GIVEN two co-managers propose identical trade (same teams, same players) within 1 hour window
WHEN second trade proposal submitted
THEN system detects duplicate via hash of (team_ids, player_ids, direction) and rejects with error: 'Identical trade already proposed by User B. View existing proposal instead.'
AND rejected user is redirected to existing proposal page
AND if trade details differ slightly (e.g., different players), both proposals are allowed (not considered duplicates)
AND trade proposal UI shows 'Proposed by: User B (Primary Manager)' to clarify originator
GIVEN commissioner or primary manager removes co-manager mid-season
WHEN co-manager removal executes

THEN system: (1) Revokes co-manager's future access to team (immediate RLS policy update), (2) Preserves all historical action records with original user_id and role, (3) Updates team management UI to show 'Former Co-Manager: User C (managed 2024-08-01 to 2024-10-15)'
AND removed co-manager receives notification: 'You have been removed as co-manager of [Team Name]. Your historical contributions remain recorded.'
AND commissioner can optionally add 'removal reason' field (stored in audit log): 'User requested removal', 'Inactive for 30+ days', 'Permission revoked by primary manager'
AND removed co-manager can still view team's public profile (if league is public) but cannot edit
GIVEN permission conflict arises (e.g., co-managers disagree on lineup decision, both submit conflicting edits)
WHEN commissioner intervenes
THEN commissioner can select 'Commissioner Override' option to force-apply a specific edit
AND override bypasses optimistic locking (no version check) and immediately applies change
AND override is logged in audit trail with: 'Commissioner [Name] overrode co-manager edits. Selected User B's lineup over User C's.'
AND all co-managers receive notification: 'Commissioner resolved edit conflict. Current lineup set by Commissioner override.'
AND UI displays 'Commissioner Override' badge on affected entity (e.g., lineup slot)
GIVEN attempt to remove last manager from team (leaving team with zero managers)
WHEN removal is attempted
THEN system prevents removal with error: 'Cannot remove last manager. Assign a new primary manager before removing User A.'
AND UI disables 'Remove' button for last manager (grayed out, tooltip explains restriction)
AND API returns 400 Bad Request with detailed message
AND audit log records failed removal attempt with reason: 'Blocked: Would create orphaned team'
GIVEN commissioner adds co-manager while primary manager simultaneously removes different co-manager
WHEN both actions occur within <1 second window
THEN database-level row locking on 'team_managers' table prevents race condition
AND both actions are queued sequentially (first to acquire lock executes, second waits)
AND both actions succeed unless constraints violated (e.g., adding duplicate co-manager)
AND audit log shows exact execution order with timestamps: 'User B added at 14:30:45.123, User C removed at 14:30:45.456'

acceptance_criteria.description: Edge Case: Primary Manager Reassignment During Active Edit
criteria: GIVEN co-manager is actively editing team (has form open, unsaved changes)
WHEN commissioner reassigns primary manager role from User A to User B
THEN system sends real-time notification to active editor: 'Primary manager changed during your edit session. Your changes will be saved as co-manager actions.'
AND active editor's unsaved changes are preserved (not lost due to role change)
AND when editor submits changes, action is attributed with new role: 'Lineup set by User A (Co-Manager)' (not Primary Manager, since role changed mid-edit)
AND if optimistic locking conflict occurs, version check still applies (role change doesn't bypass locking)
GIVEN any co-manager action (lineup change, trade proposal, roster move, team name update)
WHEN action completes

THEN audit log records: (1) action_id (UUID), (2) team_id, (3) user_id, (4) manager_role (primary/co-manager/commissioner), (5) action_type (enum), (6) before_value (JSON), (7) after_value (JSON), (8) timestamp (ISO8601), (9) version_at_time (for optimistic locking), (10) conflict_resolution_method (if applicable: 'first-wins', 'commissioner-override', 'merged')
AND audit log is append-only (no updates/deletes allowed)
AND commissioners can query audit log via dashboard: filter by team, user, action_type, date_range
AND audit log exports to CSV for external analysis (GDPR data portability)

database_schema: Add 'version' INTEGER column to 'teams' and related tables (rosters, lineups) for optimistic locking
Create 'team_managers' table with columns: team_id, user_id, role ('primary' | 'co-manager'), added_at, removed_at (nullable), removal_reason (nullable)

Create 'team_action_audit' table with columns: action_id (UUID), team_id, user_id, manager_role, action_type (ENUM), before_value (JSONB), after_value (JSONB), timestamp, version_at_time, conflict_resolution_method
Add database trigger to auto-increment 'version' on every update to teams/rosters/lineups
Add unique constraint on (team_id, user_id) in 'team_managers' table (prevent duplicate co-managers)
Add check constraint: at least one row per team_id with removed_at IS NULL (prevent orphaned teams at DB level)
api_changes: Update PUT /teams/:id endpoints to include 'version' parameter (reject if version mismatch)
Add GET /teams/:id/managers endpoint to list all managers with roles and addition dates
Add POST /teams/:id/managers endpoint to add co-manager (checks for duplicates)
Add DELETE /teams/:id/managers/:user_id endpoint to remove co-manager (enforces primary manager retention)
Add GET /teams/:id/action-history endpoint with filters: user_id, action_type, date_range
Add POST /teams/:id/commissioner-override endpoint for resolving conflicts
real_time_sync: Implement WebSocket connection for active edit sessions (send updates every 2 seconds)
Broadcast 'active-editor' events to all co-managers viewing same team
Send 'role-changed' event via WebSocket when primary manager reassigned
Implement session timeout: release 'active editor' lock after 5 minutes of inactivity
conflict_resolution: Implement merge logic for non-conflicting changes (e.g., User A changes lineup, User B changes team name - both succeed)
Use JSON diff library (e.g., jsondiffpatch) to visualize conflicting changes for users
Provide 'Reapply My Changes' button for rejected edits (pre-fills form with user's original values)
security_considerations: Verify co-manager permissions on every API call (don't cache role for >1 minute)
Use RLS policies to enforce team_managers table access (co-managers can only see their own teams)
Rate-limit team update endpoints (max 20 updates/minute per team to prevent abuse)
Encrypt audit log entries containing before_value/after_value (may include sensitive data)

requires: US-2.1 (League member roles and permissions - establishes manager role definitions)
US-2.2 (Team assignment and roster access - establishes team-user relationship)
relates_to: US-2.5 (Trade proposals and approval workflow - co-managers can propose trades, must prevent duplicates)
US-4.4 (Content history - audit trail integrates with content history views)

unit_tests: Test optimistic locking version mismatch detection
Verify permission hierarchy enforcement (primary > co-manager > commissioner)
Test trade proposal deduplication hash logic
Verify orphaned team prevention (cannot remove last manager)
integration_tests: Test concurrent edit conflict: two co-managers edit lineup simultaneously, verify first-wins and second-rejected
Test co-manager removal with historical preservation (past actions still attributed correctly)
Test commissioner override resolves conflict and logs to audit trail
Test primary manager reassignment during active edit session
edge_case_tests: Test concurrent co-manager addition/removal (database row locking)
Test active edit session when co-manager removed (verify access revocation, unsaved changes handling)
Test duplicate trade proposal detection with slight variations (e.g., different players)
Test audit trail completeness for all co-manager action types
real_time_tests: Test WebSocket 'active-editor' notifications (verify all co-managers receive updates)
Test session timeout releases 'active editor' lock after 5 minutes
Test real-time sync of form fields during concurrent edits
performance_tests: Measure optimistic locking overhead on team update latency (target: <50ms)
Test audit log write performance with 1000+ concurrent actions (target: <100ms per write)
Measure WebSocket broadcast latency for 'active-editor' events (target: <500ms)

performance: Optimistic locking adds <50ms overhead to team update operations
Audit log writes complete in <100ms per action
Real-time collaboration indicators update every 2 seconds
security: Co-manager permissions verified on every API call (no stale role caching >1 minute)
Audit log is append-only and encrypted at rest
Rate limiting: max 20 team updates/minute per team
RLS policies enforce team-manager access control
reliability: Optimistic locking prevents 100% of concurrent edit data corruption
Database constraints prevent orphaned teams (at least one manager always assigned)
Audit trail achieves 100% completeness (no missing action records)

definition_of_done: All 11 acceptance criteria pass automated tests
Optimistic locking prevents concurrent edit conflicts (first-wins, second-rejected)
Permission hierarchy enforced (primary manager > co-manager > commissioner)
Real-time collaboration indicators show active editors via WebSocket
Historical stat attribution preserved even after co-manager removal
Trade proposal deduplication prevents duplicate submissions
Commissioner override resolves conflicts and logs to audit trail
Orphaned team prevention enforced at database and API levels
Audit trail records all co-manager actions with complete metadata
Edge cases tested: concurrent addition/removal, primary manager reassignment during edit
Performance tests validate <50ms optimistic locking overhead
Documentation updated with co-manager permission model and conflict resolution
notes: Key gap: Multiple co-managers create data consistency risks without conflict detection
Optimistic locking (version field) is critical for preventing concurrent edit corruption
Real-time collaboration indicators improve UX and reduce accidental conflicts
Historical attribution must be preserved even after co-manager removal (audit compliance)
Trade proposal deduplication prevents confusion from duplicate proposals
Commissioner override provides escape hatch for unresolvable conflicts
Permission hierarchy clarifies which co-manager's actions take precedence
Database constraints (at least one manager per team) prevent orphaned teams
Audit trail completeness critical for dispute resolution and compliance
Edge cases: concurrent role changes, active edit sessions during removal, require special handling
